goals.goal: Personal-data breaches affecting customer account data and task data are detected at the data-flow boundary of the managed-cloud environment, and the moment of "becoming aware" by a designated breach-handling role is documented to anchor the Art. 33(1) 72-hour notification clock.
goals.adjustment: Scope narrowed from a generic controller to TinyTask's two data categories (customer account metadata as controller; task data as processor) at the managed-cloud data-flow boundary; the "becoming aware" documentation obligation and 72-hour clock anchor are retained in full per the corpus.

goals.goal: Relevant internal activity of the TinyTask SaaS platform — including access to or modification of task data, services, or functions — is recorded and monitored on a continuing basis throughout the product support period, with a user-visible opt-out for non-security-critical events, and any corruption or unauthorised modification is reported to the user.
goals.source: Annex I Part I (2)(l); Annex I Part II (6); Art. 13(8)
goals.adjustment: Scope narrowed from a generic manufacturer to TinyTask's B2B SaaS platform (web + mobile interface) under the CRA default product class; the user opt-out is limited to non-security-critical events; the product-internal detection layer is distinct from and does not substitute for the GDPR data-flow detection layer (DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE per CRDA-deep).
